books.description: A sweeping narrative of humanity from the Stone Age to the twenty-first century.

books.description: The riveting first-person narrative of Kvothe, a young man who grows to become the most notorious wizard his world has ever seen.

books.description: A memoir about a young girl who, kept out of school, leaves her survivalist family and goes on to earn a PhD from Cambridge.

books.title: Gone Girl

books.description: A tale of gods, kings, immortal fame, and the human heart, retelling the story of the Iliad.

books.description: A tour of the mind explaining the two systems that drive the way we think — one fast and intuitive, the other slow and deliberate.

books.title: The Long Field

books.description: A memoir of place and belonging that wanders through Wales, America, and the landscapes we carry with us.

books.title: Cloud Cuckoo Land

books.description: An intricate, time-spanning novel about a lost ancient text and the readers who protect it across centuries.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.description: Essays that review human experiences on a five-star scale, from the QWERTY keyboard to the Lascaux cave paintings.

books.title: A Line Made by Walking
books.author: Sara Baume
books.description: A quiet, precise novel about an artist retreating to her deceased grandmother's rural cottage to find a new way of seeing.

books.title: The Overstory

books.description: EpA sweeping novel about nine Americans whose unique life experiences with trees bring them together to address the destruction of forests.

books.title: Ways of Seeing
books.author: John Berger
books.description: A landmark book on how we view art, advertising, and the images that surround us in modern life.

books.title: Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.description: The epic story of Paul Atreides on the desert planet Arrakis, where spice, politics, and prophecy collide.

books.title: The Design of Everyday Things
books.author: Don Norman
books.description: A foundational guide to user-centered design, showing how the objects around us reveal the principles of good and bad design.

books.title: The Law of the Sublime
books.author: Robert Greene
books.description: From the author of The 48 Laws of Power: a guide to the sublime — the moments of awe that break us out of the narrow circle of everyday consciousness — drawn from science, history, art, and nature, with practical exercises in every chapter. Greene wrote it over seven years following his stroke.

books.title: Carry More Without Breaking
books.author: Benjamin Lavoie
books.description: For the man who's holding it all together — family, work, money, responsibility — but quietly burning out. A guide to carrying more of life's load without breaking under it. (Description drafted from the book's cover copy.)

mentalModels.name: First Principles Thinking
mentalModels.summary: Break a problem down to its most fundamental truths and reason up from there.

mentalModels.name: Compounding
mentalModels.summary: Small, consistent gains accumulate exponentially over time.

mentalModels.name: Inversion
mentalModels.summary: Solve problems backward — figure out what you want to avoid, then avoid it.

mentalModels.name: Second-Order Thinking
mentalModels.summary: Consider the consequences of the consequences, not just the immediate result.

mentalModels.name: Occam's Razor
mentalModels.summary: Among competing explanations, the simplest is usually the best.

mentalModels.name: System 1 / System 2
mentalModels.summary: The mind runs on a fast, intuitive system and a slow, deliberate one.

mentalModels.name: Loss Aversion
mentalModels.summary: Losses feel roughly twice as painful as equivalent gains feel good.

mentalModels.name: Map Is Not the Territory
mentalModels.summary: Our models of reality are not reality itself — beware confusing them.

mentalModels.name: Circle of Competence
mentalModels.summary: Know the boundaries of what you actually understand, and act inside them.

mentalModels.name: Opportunity Cost
mentalModels.summary: The true cost of a choice is the best alternative you gave up.

mentalModels.name: Hanlon's Razor
mentalModels.summary: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.

mentalModels.name: Narrative Fallacy
mentalModels.summary: We invent tidy stories to explain messy, random events after the fact.
